messages:
Emma: FYI I'm seeing a reproducible Next.js (app router) fail when importing our JS SDK from a server component that targets the edge runtime. Error is 'require is not a function' during hydration. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-internal/next-dx-repro (branch: edge-esm-interop). Jason: can you paste the stack / minimal repro steps? Emma: Minimal server component: ```js // app/page.server.jsx export default async function Page() { const mod = await import('redwood-sdk'); const client = mod?.default ?? mod; const resp = await client.generate('hello'); return
{resp}
; } ``` Works in node server but in edge runtime the bundle ends up referencing `require` and fails at runtime with hydration mismatch. Priya: Classic CJS/ESM interop. Are we publishing a CJS entrypoint that uses `module.exports =` while Next's edge bundler expects ESM? Also TS types using `export =` can confuse folks using `import` syntax. Miguel: Seen this before. Next may statically analyze and rewrite imports. If any dependency in the graph uses node built-ins at module scope (e.g., node:fs), Next will force CJS output or include fallback helpers. Do we have any server-only code imported at top-level from the SDK? Emma: Yes, one helper lib reads a config from disk during import for legacy reasons. Moving that to an async init fixed a local variant. But the `require is not a function` still happens for the ESM/CJS default interop. Jason: Two-pronged solution: (1) ship an ESM-first build with `export default` + named exports and an explicit `exports` map in package.json; (2) provide a small CJS shim that `module.exports = require('./esm').default` so old consumers keep working. That pattern avoids `module.exports = { default: ... }` pitfalls. Priya: For TS: add an index.d.ts that declares `export default` for the main client, and set "types" in package.json to point at it. Also add `typesVersions` if we need mappings for old TS. That will make `import client from 'redwood-sdk'` type correctly in ESM projects. Miguel: We should also add a CI sample that builds a minimal Next app targeting the edge and runs a smoke test. A rollback-proof approach is to include an example in `examples/next-app-router-edge-esm` that shows: no top-level node: imports, dynamic import pattern, and `const client = mod?.default ?? mod`. Emma: Could adding "type": "module" to our ESM package break anyone? We'd need publishing strategy: publish `dist/esm` with package.json exports `{ ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }`. Jason: Yep. And update the build pipeline to emit both ESM and CJS bundles. Rollout in two steps: publish ESM behind a beta tag, see if next examples break, then full release. Priya: I'll draft the PR to change exports + add index.d.ts. Also will add a short section in SDK docs: "Next.js app-router & edge runtime: avoid server-only imports at module scope; prefer dynamic import interop pattern." CI Bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-internal/sdk/pull/801 (wip) failing tests on node 14/16. Emma: Thanks. I'll add the repro screenshots and a short checklist to the PR: verify example builds in Next 13.4+, verify edge runtime smoke test passes, and update changelog. Miguel: One more DX note: show a suggested babel/tsconfig snippet for consumers who still need CJS interop. And a tiny runtime helper `interopDefault(mod)` we can ship as `import { interopDefault } from 'redwood-sdk/runtime'` to make customer code nicer. Priya: Good idea. Action items: 1) PR for exports + types (Priya). 2) Examples folder and CI job for Next edge (Emma). 3) Small runtime helper and docs snippet (Miguel). 4) Beta publish and compatibility smoke tests (Jason). Emma: Sweet. We'll keep the repro branch until PR lands. Thanks :thumbsup:
